name: Mehida
overview: Mehida was a male Levite who served as a temple servant, a role that involved duties related to the worship and maintenance of the temple. His identity as a member of the tribe of Levi aligns with the biblical designation of Levites as those set apart for religious service. There are no additional notes recorded about him beyond his temple service.
namesAndTitles: The name Mehida is a proper name mentioned in Scripture, with a possible meaning of 'bought as slave.' This meaning may reflect the historical context of Levites who were dedicated to God's service, but the name itself was not given by God according to the record.
familyAndRelationships: Mehida is identified as a descendant of Levi, connecting him to the priestly tribe set apart for temple duties. Scripture does not provide further family relationships beyond this tribal affiliation.
scriptureSignificance: Mehida's significance lies in his role as a temple servant, which underscores the importance of the Levites in maintaining the worship and function of the temple community. His mention in Ezra 2:52 highlights the restoration and organization of the temple servants following the Babylonian exile, reflecting God's faithfulness in preserving His chosen servants and their sacred duties.
